name: Question 3
problem:
Determine all real eigenvalues $\lambda $ of the matrix 
$P=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 4 \\ 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 4 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}].$
worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,P-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
P-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & 2 & 4 \\ 2 & -\lambda  & 2 \\ 4 & 2 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is given by $det(P-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Expanding the determinant across the $1$st row, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(P-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & 2 & 4 \\ 2 & -\lambda  & 2 \\ 4 & 2 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-\lambda  & 2 \\ 2 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}|-2|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 4 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}|+4|\begin{aligned}2 & -\lambda  \\ 4 & 2\end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-{\lambda }^{3}+6{\lambda }^{2}-5\lambda -12)-2(-2-2\lambda )+4(4+4\lambda ) & =0 \\ -{\lambda }^{3}+6{\lambda }^{2}+15\lambda +8 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{3}-6{\lambda }^{2}-15\lambda -8 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to solve this equation. We find the first root by testing some values. According to the rational zeros theorem, a list of good first guesses consists of all divisors of $8:$ 

$$
\pm 1,\pm 2,\pm 4,\pm 8
$$

- Let's pick $x=1.$ Substituting to the characteristic equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(1)^{3}-6(1)^{2}-15(1)-8 & =-28.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $\lambda =1$ is not a root of the equation.

- Let's pick $x=-1.$ Substituting to the characteristic equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(-1)^{3}-6(-1)^{2}-15(-1)-8 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $\lambda =-1$ is a root of the equation.

So, we can factor $(\lambda +1)$ out of ${\lambda }^{3}-6{\lambda }^{2}-15\lambda -8$ using synthetic division:

| $-1$ | $1$ | $-6$ | $-15$ | $-8$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | $↓$ | $-1$ | $7$ | $8$ |
|  | $1$ | $-7$ | $-8$ | $0$ |

So, we obtain the following factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}(\lambda +1)({\lambda }^{2}-7\lambda -8) & =0 \\ (\lambda +1)(\lambda +1)(\lambda -8) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1}=-1,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{2}=8.$

Question 3
?

Determine all real eigenvalues λ of the matrix P=[324202423].

a
λ∈{−1,2,4}
b
λ∈{−1,8}
c
λ∈{1,8}
d
λ∈{−1,−2,4}
e
λ∈{−1,1,−8}
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we find the matrix P−λI: ﻿﻿﻿P−λI=[3−λ242−λ2423−λ]

The characteristic equation is given by det(P−λI)=0.

Expanding the determinant across the 1st row, we get the following:

det(P−λI)=0|3−λ242−λ2423−λ|=0(3−λ)|−λ223−λ|−2|2243−λ|+4|2−λ42|=0(−λ3+6λ2−5λ−12)−2(−2−2λ)+4(4+4λ)=0−λ3+6λ2+15λ+8=0λ3−6λ2−15λ−8=0

Now, we need to solve this equation. We find the first root by testing some values. According to the rational zeros theorem, a list of good first guesses consists of all divisors of 8: ±1,±2,±4,±8

  • Let's pick x=1. Substituting to the characteristic equation gives (1)3−6(1)2−15(1)−8=−28. Hence, λ=1 is not a root of the equation.

  • Let's pick x=−1. Substituting to the characteristic equation gives (−1)3−6(−1)2−15(−1)−8=0. Hence, λ=−1 is a root of the equation.

So, we can factor (λ+1) out of λ3−6λ2−15λ−8 using synthetic division:

−1 1 −6 −15 −8
↓ −1 7 8
1 −7 −8 0

So, we obtain the following factorization: (λ+1)(λ2−7λ−8)=0(λ+1)(λ+1)(λ−8)=0

Therefore, the eigenvalues are λ1=−1, and λ2=8.
